reflections.summary: Team-preview failure: brought Houndoom and Sneasler but never deployed them, leaving Pelipper+Toxapex as the only functional core against a Ghost/Fairy-heavy opponent squad. Toxapex alone could not pressure Basculegion (Water resists Water) or withstand sustained Dragapult Shadow Ball chip plus Floette-Eternal's late-game Moonblast cleanup. Pelipper's rain was wasted without offensive Water abusers that could threaten the opponent, and Protect chains on turns 6-7 ceded tempo while Dragapult free
reflections.adjustment: For game 3, lead Houndoom alongside Toxapex (or Pelipper) to threaten Basculegion with Dark Pulse and absorb Arcanine-Hisui's FlareBlitz if it appears. Drop Sneasler from the bring-four against this squad—it's too frail versus Dragapult/Floette and Unburden never got to proc. Prioritize KOing Basculegion early with Houndoom before it accumulates Last Respects boosts, and save Toxapex's Haze for after Annihilape is confirmed absent or after its Defiant has already triggered.
reflections.notebook: Opponent durable tendencies: leads Basculegion+Dragapult, Dragapult Choice-locks Shadow Ball and spams it into the same target, Basculegion Protects at low HP, Floette-Eternal enters late as cleanup with Moonblast/Light of Ruin, Maushold uses Friend Guard to reduce ally damage. Revealed facts: Basculegion is Adamant Adaptability Life Orb (Water resists Water, so Toxapex Chilling Water cannot OHKO from full), Dragapult is Timid Scarf Infiltrator, Floette-Eternal is Modest Flower Veil with Floettite, Annihilape is Defiant Adamant Leftovers (avoid Haze on its switch-in), Arcanine-Hisui is Jolly Intimidate Expert Belt. Future plans: bring a Dark-type (Houndoom) as primary Basculegion/Floette answer; consider a Normal-type immune to Ghost spam if available; do not bring Sneasler into Ghost+Fairy-heavy lineups; use Pelipper rain only when paired with an offensive Water or Electric abuser that pressures Water resists.
